subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart message-preservation design should be the canonical path for this issue: SQLite followup queue recovery, SIGUSR1 drain mitigation, or a broader channel/session recovery program?
rationale: Current source confirms the bug, but repository policy makes persistent state and channel ownership compatibility-sensitive, and multiple open PRs cover overlapping but different fix boundaries.

options.title: Advance SQLite followup recovery
options.body: Rework or land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a successor that persists followup queues in shared SQLite with focused upgrade and live channel proof.

options.title: Land SIGUSR1 mitigation only
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 to reduce debounce and mid-drain loss during in-process reloads while leaving downtime catch-up as separate work.

options.title: Fold into broader recovery
options.body: Treat this as part of the larger graceful restart/session recovery design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57425, accepting that the narrow queue fix will wait.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite followup recovery
recommendation.body: Rework or land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a successor that persists followup queues in shared SQLite with focused upgrade and live channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central-line blame and issue mentions point to steipete as the best available owner to choose the product boundary.
